headline: Kanlaon Remains at Alert Level 2 as Authorities Reinforce Ashfall Precautions
seoTitle: Kanlaon Alert Level 2: Ashfall Precautions Reinforced | FMB News
seoDescription: Kanlaon remains under Alert Level 2, with residents advised to stay outside the 4-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone and protect themselves if ashfall occurs.
deck: Kanlaon remains in a state of increased unrest, with the four-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone still off-limits and communities advised to protect themselves during ashfall events.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Kanlaon Volcano remains under Alert Level 2 as authorities continue monitoring unrest and reminding communities on Negros Island about ashfall precautions.

PHIVOLCS guidance under Alert Level 2 says shallow magmatic processes continue beneath the volcano and that sudden explosive activity remains possible. The public is strongly advised not to enter the four-kilometer-radius Permanent Danger Zone.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Recent PHIVOLCS-sourced monitoring summarized by the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program recorded repeated ash emissions during August while Alert Level 2 remained in force. PHIVOLCS also advises people affected by ashfall to cover their nose and mouth with a clean damp cloth or dust mask and warns pilots against flying close to the summit.

The approved August 22 FMB News brief reported new episodic ash plumes and local ashfall precautions. Because a same-day primary bulletin containing every locality-specific detail was not independently retrievable in this run, those details are not overstated here.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Ash can irritate the eyes and respiratory system, affect crops and water supplies, and create aviation hazards. Communities near channels draining the volcano also need to remain alert during heavy rain because volcanic deposits can be remobilized into sediment-laden flows.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow PHIVOLCS and local disaster offices for changes in alert level, ashfall direction, sulfur dioxide measurements and any expanded evacuation or health guidance.
